k: ...Was he there? A boy, nine, with a gap in his teeth? Tam. His name is Tam.
src: '...Was he there? A boy, nine, with a gap in his teeth? Tam. His name is Tam.'

k: No. Don't tell me. I've decided I'm going home.
src: 'No. Don\'t tell me. I\'ve decided I\'m going home.'

k: My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.
src: 'My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.'

k: The Choir says when the Hierophant's work is done the gate will open, and I'll see him at the festival. I've been waiting since the spring.
src: 'The Choir says when the Hierophant\'s work is done the gate will open, and I\'ll see him at the festival. I\'ve been waiting since the spring.'

k: Is it still spring? I've lost count. Nothing changes up here. That's the point, they say.
src: 'Is it still spring? I\'ve lost count. Nothing changes up here. That\'s the point, they say.'

k: Eleven months I've sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.
src: 'Eleven months I\'ve sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.'

k: Some nights I can hear her laughing, through the wall. Same laugh. Same moment. Over and over.
src: 'Some nights I can hear her laughing, through the wall. Same laugh. Same moment. Over and over.'

k: I tell myself that's a comfort.
src: 'I tell myself that\'s a comfort.'

k: They say inside it's always the best day of your life. Isn't that what we all want? Isn't that what everyone has ever wanted?
src: 'They say inside it\'s always the best day of your life. Isn\'t that what we all want? Isn\'t that what everyone has ever wanted?'

k: I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.
src: 'I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.'

k: ...You sound very tired.
src: '...You sound very tired.'

k: I am. That's how I know I'm still alive.
src: 'I am. That\'s how I know I\'m still alive.'

k: You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.
src: 'You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.'

k: The big gate never opens. Don't bother knocking; I knocked for a week.
src: 'The big gate never opens. Don\'t bother knocking; I knocked for a week.'

k: But the white ships bring crates round the east side of the plaza. There's a lift. A man with a spear stands by it and says "halt" a lot.
src: 'But the white ships bring crates round the east side of the plaza. There\'s a lift. A man with a spear stands by it and says "halt" a lot.'

k: Supply line
src: 'Supply line'

k: The great gate of the Spire is sealed with gold. Carved over it, in letters as tall as Pip:
src: 'The great gate of the Spire is sealed with gold. Carved over it, in letters as tall as Pip:'

k: AND THE GOOD DAY SHALL NOT END.
src: 'AND THE GOOD DAY SHALL NOT END.'

k: A statue of the Hierophant, arms open, smiling. Someone has left a child's shoe at its feet. Then another. Then hundreds.
src: 'A statue of the Hierophant, arms open, smiling. Someone has left a child\'s shoe at its feet. Then another. Then hundreds.'

k: A statue of a little girl in a festival dress, holding a ribbon. There is no name on the plinth.
src: 'A statue of a little girl in a festival dress, holding a ribbon. There is no name on the plinth.'

k: The pilgrims' fire. Nobody needs it for warmth up here. They keep it lit so there is something that changes.
src: 'The pilgrims\' fire. Nobody needs it for warmth up here. They keep it lit so there is something that changes.'

k: The lift's guarded.
src: 'The lift\'s guarded.'

k: Clock
src: 'Clock'

k: Clock-cases, floor to ceiling. Each face is painted with the same summer sky. Each one has stopped at noon.
src: 'Clock-cases, floor to ceiling. Each face is painted with the same summer sky. Each one has stopped at noon.'

k: A clock with a child's drawing tucked into its glass: a girl, a boy, a big yellow sun, and the word ALWAYS.
src: 'A clock with a child\'s drawing tucked into its glass: a girl, a boy, a big yellow sun, and the word ALWAYS.'

k: The Noon Gate. Warm air breathes through it, smelling of honey and cut grass.
src: 'The Noon Gate. Warm air breathes through it, smelling of honey and cut grass.'

k: Not back. Never back. East — the balcony.
src: 'Not back. Never back. East — the balcony.'

k: Lift shaft's full of light! East, sparrow — the balcony!
src: 'Lift shaft\'s full of light! East, sparrow — the balcony!'

k: THE HALCYON — Capt. C. Ashe.nGangplank. Mind the gap. The gap is the whole sky.
src: 'THE HALCYON — Capt. C. Ashe.\nGangplank. Mind the gap. The gap is the whole sky.'

k: Look west
src: 'Look west'

k: The bow cuts through cloud the color of a bruise. Below: nothing at all, for a very long way.
src: 'The bow cuts through cloud the color of a bruise. Below: nothing at all, for a very long way.'

k: The mainmast. Someone has carved PIP into it at a height that suggests standing on a barrel. Below it, smaller: CORVIN SAYS NO.
src: 'The mainmast. Someone has carved PIP into it at a height that suggests standing on a barrel. Below it, smaller: CORVIN SAYS NO.'

k: The foremast. A patched sail, a patched patch, and a single kite tangled in the rigging.
src: 'The foremast. A patched sail, a patched patch, and a single kite tangled in the rigging.'

k: Forge
src: 'Forge'

k: Corvin's chart table. Under the charts, a small painting of a woman in a Dawnguard sky-wing coat, laughing at whoever held the brush. On the back: "H.M. — don't you DARE frame this." It is framed.
src: 'Corvin\'s chart table. Under the charts, a small painting of a woman in a Dawnguard sky-wing coat, laughing at whoever held the brush. On the back: "H.M. — don\'t you DARE frame this." It is framed.'

k: Corvin's books: "Navigation for the Reluctant," "Debts and How to Outlive Them," and a much-read book of children's bedtime stories with the price still on it.
src: 'Corvin\'s books: "Navigation for the Reluctant," "Debts and How to Outlive Them," and a much-read book of children\'s bedtime stories with the price still on it.'

k: Ilse's stove. Something is simmering. It smells like home, if home were mostly onions.
src: 'Ilse\'s stove. Something is simmering. It smells like home, if home were mostly onions.'

k: Ilse's shelf: bandages rolled tight, tinctures labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One jar just says: PIP. NO.
src: 'Ilse\'s shelf: bandages rolled tight, tinctures labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One jar just says: PIP. NO.'

k: Nell's forge, built into the ship's boiler. It runs on coal, spite and, lately, the heat of a Sun Shard on a long chain.
src: 'Nell\'s forge, built into the ship\'s boiler. It runs on coal, spite and, lately, the heat of a Sun Shard on a long chain.'

k: THE KEEPER'S HOURSnThe sun wakes in the east. At noon it stands above us. At evening it goes home to the west.nRing the hours as the sun walks them, and the Lantern will hear you.
src: 'THE KEEPER\'S HOURS\nThe sun wakes in the east. At noon it stands above us. At evening it goes home to the west.\nRing the hours as the sun walks them, and the Lantern will hear you.'

k: Bell
src: 'Bell'

k: Glass wall
src: 'Glass wall'

k: A wall of glass has grown across the bridge, clear as still water and hard as a vow. Something in the garden below must open it.
src: 'A wall of glass has grown across the bridge, clear as still water and hard as a vow. Something in the garden below must open it.'

k: A nomad's water barrel. On the lid, a tally scratched with a knife: one notch for every day. The notches stop on the day the sun broke. Beside them, in a child's hand: STILL HERE. STILL HERE. STILL HERE. Then nothing.
src: 'A nomad\'s water barrel. On the lid, a tally scratched with a knife: one notch for every day. The notches stop on the day the sun broke. Beside them, in a child\'s hand: STILL HERE. STILL HERE. STILL HERE. Then nothing.'

k: A caravan tent, its poles fused into the glass. Inside, a bedroll, a cold teapot and a child's sandal. Whoever lived here packed in a hurry and left the important things.
src: 'A caravan tent, its poles fused into the glass. Inside, a bedroll, a cold teapot and a child\'s sandal. Whoever lived here packed in a hurry and left the important things.'

k: A Choir pilgrim, still in her traveling sandals, facing the Lantern. She came all this way to hear the Dawnsong one last time.
src: 'A Choir pilgrim, still in her traveling sandals, facing the Lantern. She came all this way to hear the Dawnsong one last time.'

k: A wall of blue ice seals the stair. Deep inside it, the shadow of a monk's hand, pressed flat, as if he had tried to hold the avalanche back.
src: 'A wall of blue ice seals the stair. Deep inside it, the shadow of a monk\'s hand, pressed flat, as if he had tried to hold the avalanche back.'

k: More ice. Above it, very faintly, a voice reciting the same short prayer over and over.
src: 'More ice. Above it, very faintly, a voice reciting the same short prayer over and over.'

k: A cairn of stones. On the top stone, in charcoal that the snow has somehow never touched: HALVARD. A monk's prayer-cord is wrapped around it. Someone came back for him.
src: 'A cairn of stones. On the top stone, in charcoal that the snow has somehow never touched: HALVARD. A monk\'s prayer-cord is wrapped around it. Someone came back for him.'

k: Through a cracked shutter: a monk's cell. A cot, a candle stub, and a table covered in drawings of a tuning fork, each with a single note crossed out.
src: 'Through a cracked shutter: a monk\'s cell. A cot, a candle stub, and a table covered in drawings of a tuning fork, each with a single note crossed out.'

k: The refectory. Forty bowls set out on a long table, forty spoons beside them. The soup froze a year ago. No one sat down.
src: 'The refectory. Forty bowls set out on a long table, forty spoons beside them. The soup froze a year ago. No one sat down.'

k: The monastery bell lies split in the snow. It rang the hours on this mountain for six hundred years. Then it rang the avalanche.
src: 'The monastery bell lies split in the snow. It rang the hours on this mountain for six hundred years. Then it rang the avalanche.'

k: The village well. A bucket on a rope. The water at the bottom is perfectly clear: the only clean water in Mirefen. Osk kept it that way to the end.
src: 'The village well. A bucket on a rope. The water at the bottom is perfectly clear: the only clean water in Mirefen. Osk kept it that way to the end.'

k: Through the window of the stilt-house: rows of cots, each one neatly made, each one empty. A chalkboard: NAME / HOUR / MEDICINE, filled in until the chalk ran out, then filled in with charcoal, then with a burnt stick.
src: 'Through the window of the stilt-house: rows of cots, each one neatly made, each one empty. A chalkboard: NAME / HOUR / MEDICINE, filled in until the chalk ran out, then filled in with charcoal, then with a burnt stick.'

k: A child's wooden boat on the windowsill, carved with more love than skill. Painted on the side: FOR MOTHER OSK, WHO MADE ME BETTER.
src: 'A child\'s wooden boat on the windowsill, carved with more love than skill. Painted on the side: FOR MOTHER OSK, WHO MADE ME BETTER.'

k: Osk's hut. Herbs hang from every beam. On the door, a list of names in her neat hand, each one crossed out, gently, with a single line.
src: 'Osk\'s hut. Herbs hang from every beam. On the door, a list of names in her neat hand, each one crossed out, gently, with a single line.'

k: Shrine
src: 'Shrine'

k: Thorns
src: 'Thorns'

k: Carved inside the hollow oak, at a child's height: LYSA WAS HERE. Below it, in a careful, very old hand: SO WAS ELOWEN.
src: 'Carved inside the hollow oak, at a child\'s height: LYSA WAS HERE. Below it, in a careful, very old hand: SO WAS ELOWEN.'

k: A cherry tree, still in blossom. The only living thing in the court. Petals fall and do not land; they hang in the air, as if waiting to be told what to do.
src: 'A cherry tree, still in blossom. The only living thing in the court. Petals fall and do not land; they hang in the air, as if waiting to be told what to do.'

k: Lightning rod
src: 'Lightning rod'

k: A ward of raw lightning hangs across the bridge, humming like a hive. Your hair stands on end from three paces away.
src: 'A ward of raw lightning hangs across the bridge, humming like a hive. Your hair stands on end from three paces away.'
